summary:
Orbit Architect is an interactive 2D aerospace engineering and rocket simulation tool built in Unity. Players act as mission architects, designing multi-stage rockets and payload instruments within strict real-world engineering constraints (TWR thresholds, mass ratios, and budget caps) inspired by NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT).

Players progress through sequential launch missions—ranging from automated Earth satellite deployments and Mars rover landing sequences to crewed lunar surface excursions—balancing Tsiolkovsky delta-V calculations and vis-viva orbital mechanics before executing live physics-based launches complete with stage separations, atmospheric drag penalties, and zero-G orbit rotations.
details:
The project is a small game with repeatable missions that is intended to teach anyone the basic principles of space mission design, not through bulk explanation, but their own trial and error. The game uses some intuitive rocket parts and instruments to display themes and concepts rather than perfect physics.

The project does fail to match up to a physics-based, scientifically backed simulation, like GMAT, but its largest benefit is its simplicity. It can portray basic concepts easily for anyone to understand. Space missions are complicated and take massive budgets and complicated planning. This game doesn't show all of the details, but it can introduce the complexity in a simple way while still preserving some of the key details. We wanted to keep the game realistic while not losing the simplicity that would allow the game to be accessible to anyone.

We utilized Unity, so the game is coded in C#. For the creation of sprites, we utilized Aesprite. The game utilizes hand drawn art for everything giving the game a unique look. In order to assist with bulk coding, we utilized Gemini 4 Hydrogen. For the logic and math behind the code, that was pulled from GMAT, either by utilizing equations from the simulations or by using the simulation data as the default stats or patterns to follow within the game.
